userStories.title: Emit pi-ai's completed tool arguments
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make final tool-call events use pi-ai's completed argument object after the accumulated deltas successfully parse.

**Motivation** — With the arguments only on `response.output_item.done`, pi-ai's final message held `KL` but nax returned empty input.

**Approach** — The `toolcall_end` case of `createPiProtocol(...).stream` (`packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-client.ts`).
Target: the parse-failure path is unchanged. When the accumulation parses, `input` is `event.toolCall.arguments` if `event.toolCall.argumentsError` is absent and `event.toolCall.arguments` is a non-null, non-array object; otherwise `input` is the parsed accumulation, as today.

pi-ai 1.5.0 (`@earendil-works/pi-ai`, read through `pi-client.ts` only): a `toolcall_end` event's `toolCall` is `{ id, name, arguments: JsonObject, argumentsError?: string }`, where `argumentsError` is set when the completed arguments text was not a JSON object (then `arguments` is `{}`).

`packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/tool-args.ts`: `createToolArgAccumulator()`, `parseToolArgs(raw)` (an empty string parses to `{}`; otherwise `JSON.parse`).

Keep the malformed-arguments drain's terminal usage and single bad-request behavior. The accumulated tool-argument text is not JSON: Unchanged: `bad-request` `Tool "<name>" returned unparseable arguments.`, after the terminal usage. pi-ai marks the completed arguments with `argumentsError` but the accumulation parses: The parsed accumulation is used, as today.

**Scope** — In: the toolcall_end input selection and new completed-argument regression tests in `packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/pi-client-final-args.test.ts`. Existing tool-argument tests remain unchanged. Out: terminal thinking buffering (US-002), HTTP observation (US-003), credential storage (US-004), and picker filtering (US-005). A custom (grammar) tool call is not given separate handling; its `toolcall_end` takes `toolCall.arguments` under the same rule as a JSON call. US-001 only: no AC covers deltas that parse to a non-empty object while `toolCall.arguments` is `{}` with no `argumentsError`; pi-ai 1.5.0 replaces the delta text only when the completed item's arguments are non-empty, so it does not produce that state, and the rule then emits `{}`. A tool call whose accumulated delta text is not JSON still ends the stream with the `bad-request` error, even when pi-ai's completed arguments are valid. No live test is added.

**Interface** — `createPiProtocol(...).stream`; `toolCallAt(partial, index)`; `createToolArgAccumulator()`; `parseToolArgs(raw)`; completed `toolCall`: `{ id, name, arguments: JsonObject, argumentsError?: string }`.

Verification uses scripted pi-ai events via the existing fakePi/message/drain pattern and the real-pi client (createClient, defaultProviders(), transportRetries:0, memory openai API-key store, and a protocols factory returning defaultProtocols({ credentials, providerOverrides })); select await client.model("openai", "gpt-5.4"). A tool call t1 has id t1 and name lookup. The local fetch SSE harness must deliver each event in its own macrotask, never enqueue all terminal data together. Demonstrate the new regressions fail against the old code; normal-delta and malformed-delta controls already pass.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] When toolcall_delta events carry {"city":"SG"} and toolcall_end.toolCall.arguments is { city: "KL" } with no argumentsError, draining createPiProtocol("openai-responses", deps).stream(request) yields a tool-call for id t1, name lookup, with input { city: "KL" }.
[unit] When no toolcall_delta arrives and toolcall_end.toolCall.arguments is { city: "KL" }, draining yields a tool-call for t1 with input { city: "KL" }.
[unit] (control) When toolcall_delta events carry {"city":"KL"} and toolCall.arguments is { city: "KL" }, draining yields a tool-call for t1 with input { city: "KL" }.
[unit] When toolcall_delta events carry {"city":"SG"} and toolcall_end.toolCall has arguments {} and argumentsError set, draining yields a tool-call for t1 with input { city: "SG" }.

[unit] (control) When toolcall_delta events carry {"city" and toolCall.arguments is { city: "KL" }, draining ends with an error event of kind bad-request and message Tool "lookup" returned unparseable arguments.
[unit] (control) In that malformed case, draining yields no tool-call event.

[integration] Through the real-pi client, when fetch streams response.output_item.added for function call fc_1 (call id c1, name lookup) with empty arguments, then response.output_item.done for that call with arguments {"city":"KL"}, then response.completed whose response.output holds that completed call, client.complete resolves with toolCalls[0].input equal to { city: "KL" }.

[integration] Through the real-pi client, when fetch streams the same call with an argument delta {"city":"SG"}, then response.output_item.done with arguments {"city":"KL"}, then response.completed holding the completed call, client.complete resolves with toolCalls[0].input equal to { city: "KL" }.

[unit; failure handling] (control) When malformed accumulated tool-argument text is followed by a terminal event carrying usage on a non-aborted request, draining emits that terminal usage before the final bad-request error, unchanged from existing malformed-arguments behavior.

routing.reasoning: A bounded stream-mapping change plus a new unit/real-pi local-fetch suite; preserve malformed-delta behavior and prove terminal argument authority before implementation.

userStories.title: Flush thinking blocks with terminal reasoning signatures
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Defer complete thinking blocks until stream termination so successful responses include pi-ai's terminal signatures for stateless replay.

**Motivation** — With `encrypted_content` only in `response.completed`, pi-ai's final message held it (pi-ai backfills it in `finalizeResponse`), but the replay omitted it.

**Approach** — The `thinking_end` and terminal cases of `createPiProtocol(...).stream`.
Target: `thinking_end` holds the block, with its content index, instead of emitting it. The held blocks are emitted in the order their `thinking_end` events arrived:
1. On `done`, before the `usage` event. For each held block, `thinkingBlockAt(event.message, contentIndex)` is read; its `signature` replaces the held signature when present, and its `redacted` replaces the held flag when present. A field absent from the terminal block keeps the held value. The text is always the `thinking_end` text.
2. On every other end of the stream (an `error` event, the malformed-arguments drain ending on `done` or `error`, a stream that ends with no terminal event, and a thrown failure), the held blocks are emitted with their `thinking_end` values, before the first event that path emits (`usage` or `error`). When the request was aborted, the flush is skipped: an aborted `error` event still emits its `usage` (when non-zero) and rethrows the abort as today, and a thrown failure on an aborted request rethrows it as today, in both cases without emitting the held blocks.
Signatures stay opaque: they are copied, never compared or inspected.

On a non-aborted request, when the stream ends on an error, a drain or a throw while thinking blocks are held, the held blocks are emitted with their `thinking_end` values before the terminal events. The abort exception above takes precedence: no held thinking blocks are emitted on the aborted error or thrown-failure paths.

`packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-client.ts`: `thinkingBlockAt(partial, index)` returns `{ signature?, redacted? }` read off the thinking block at a content index; `toolCallAt(partial, index)`.
`packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/collect.ts`: `collectStream` pushes every `thinking` event's block into `CompleteResult.thinking` in arrival order; `ProtocolStreamError` carries the `error` event's payload as `protocolError`.

**Scope** — In: all complete-thinking flush paths in pi-client.ts and new held-thinking/local replay tests in `packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/pi-client-terminal-thinking.test.ts`. Keep the US-001 final-tool-argument change. Existing thinking_end tests remain unchanged. Out: final-tool-input rules (US-001), fetch observation (US-003), file-store validation/locking (US-004), and catalog filtering (US-005). `thinking-delta` events are still emitted as they arrive; only the complete `thinking` block moves to the end of the stream. No live test is added.

**Interface** — `createPiProtocol(...).stream`; `thinkingBlockAt(partial, index)` returns `{ signature?, redacted? }`; `collectStream`; `CompleteResult.thinking`.

Unit cases use createPiProtocol("openai-responses", deps) and the existing fakePi/message/drain patterns. Separate early partial and terminal message objects so the test does not accidentally depend on pi-ai mutating one object. The real-pi client uses createClient with defaultProviders(), transportRetries:0, a memory credential store holding an openai API key, and a protocols factory returning defaultProtocols({ credentials, providerOverrides }); select await client.model("openai", "gpt-5.4"). Deliver each stubbed SSE event in a separate macrotask. Replay the first CompleteResult.thinking on the next assistant message and inspect the second request body, rather than inspecting an internally synthesized signature. Strict three-session TDD protects opaque encrypted-signature replay; demonstrate the terminal-backfill regression fails on baseline and retain the early-signature control.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] When thinking_end at content index 0 has content hmm and event.partial.content[0] is a thinking block with thinkingSignature sig-early, and the done event's message is a separate object whose content[0] is a thinking block with thinkingSignature sig-final, draining yields exactly one thinking event whose block is { text: "hmm", signature: "sig-final" }.
[unit] When thinking_end at index 0 is followed by toolcall_delta and toolcall_end for t1 at index 1 and then done, the yielded event types end with tool-call, thinking, usage, done in that order.

[unit] (control) When the thinking block at event.partial.content[event.contentIndex] on thinking_end has thinkingSignature sig-early and redacted false, and the done event's message.content holds either no block or a text block at that same index, the thinking event's block is { text: "hmm", signature: "sig-early", redacted: false }.

[unit] When the thinking block at event.partial.content[event.contentIndex] on thinking_end has redacted false and no signature, and the done event's message.content at that same index is a thinking block with redacted true and thinkingSignature opaque, the thinking event's block is { text: "hmm", signature: "opaque", redacted: true }.
[unit] When two thinking_end events arrive at content indexes 0 and 2 with texts a and b, draining yields two thinking events with texts a then b.
[unit] (control) When thinking_end is followed by a pi-ai error event with message upstream failed, draining yields the thinking event with its thinking_end values before the final error event.
[unit] (control) When thinking_end is followed by the end of scripted events without a terminal event, draining yields the thinking event with its thinking_end values.
[unit] (control) When thinking_end is followed by a malformed tool-call delta {"city" and then done, draining yields the thinking event before usage.
[unit] (control) When thinking_end is followed by a malformed tool-call delta {"city" and then done, draining ends with the bad-request error.
[unit] (control) When the scripted stream throws new Error("socket reset") after thinking_end, draining yields the thinking event before the final error event.
[unit] When the request signal is already aborted and thinking_end is followed by a pi-ai error with message Request was aborted, iterating rejects with the signal's abort reason.
[unit] When the request signal is already aborted and thinking_end is followed by a pi-ai error event with message Request was aborted, iterating the stream yields no thinking event.

[integration] Through the real-pi client, when response one streams response.output_item.added for reasoning item rs_1, then response.output_item.done for rs_1 with a summary and no encrypted_content, then response.completed whose output holds rs_1 with encrypted_content opaque-fixture, each in its own macrotask, a second client.complete replaying the first result's thinking on an assistant message sends a request body with store false.
[integration] In that two-request sequence, the second request body's input holds reasoning item rs_1 with encrypted_content opaque-fixture.

[integration] (control) Through the real-pi client, when response one's response.output_item.done for rs_1 already carries encrypted_content opaque-fixture, a second client.complete replaying the first result's thinking sends a request whose reasoning item rs_1 has encrypted_content opaque-fixture.
[unit; failure handling] When a pi-ai error after thinking_end reports non-zero usage on a non-aborted request, the held thinking event with its thinking_end values precedes the usage event.

[unit; failure handling] On a non-aborted request, when the malformed-arguments drain ends on pi-ai error while thinking is held, the held thinking event with its thinking_end values precedes the first terminal usage or error event.

[unit; failure handling] On a non-aborted request, when the malformed-arguments drain ends on done with terminal thinking metadata different from the held metadata, the emitted thinking block retains its thinking_end values.

[unit; abort handling] (control) When an aborted pi-ai error reports non-zero usage after thinking_end, iteration emits that usage before rethrowing the abort, unchanged from existing billed-usage behavior.
[unit; abort handling] (control) When the stream throws after thinking_end on an aborted request, iteration rethrows the same thrown failure as today.
[unit; abort handling] When the stream throws after thinking_end on an already-aborted request, iteration yields no held thinking blocks.

routing.reasoning: The change is bounded buffering and exit-path flushing in one existing protocol module using thinkingBlockAt, not a new cross-module abstraction; replay of opaque encrypted/signed reasoning retains the security-override three-session isolation despite medium complexity.

userStories.title: Preserve HTTP error status and Retry-After before SDK processing
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Observe failed HTTP responses at fetch time so the existing error mapper retains status and numeric Retry-After.

**Motivation** — Injected 429 and 503 responses with `Retry-After: 41` kept their status but lost the header, and `turnRetryDelayMs` chose 1 second.

**Approach** — `createPiDeps(...).stream` (`packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-client.ts`).
Target: also passes `fetch: observeErrorResponses(onResponse)`. The `onResponse` option stays as it is.

New `observeErrorResponses(onResponse)` in new file `packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/error-response-fetch.ts`. It imports nothing from pi-ai (`check:pi-ai-imports`) and no Bun API (`check:no-bun-apis`).
Target: returns a function with the signature of `globalThis.fetch`. Each call forwards its arguments to `globalThis.fetch`, read at call time (so a test stub installed after construction is used). When the returned `Response` has a status of 400 or above, it calls `onResponse({ status, headers })` with the headers as a plain record of the response's header names and values, then returns the same `Response` untouched. A response below 400 is returned without calling `onResponse`. A rejected `fetch` rejects with the same reason, without calling `onResponse`.
Effect: on an HTTP error, `observed` holds the error response, so the existing `error` case reads `status` and `retryAfter` from it. When pi-ai retries a failed request and the retry succeeds, pi-ai's own `onResponse` call overwrites `observed`, as today.

pi-ai 1.5.0 (`@earendil-works/pi-ai`, read through `pi-client.ts` only): `SimpleStreamOptions.fetch` is honoured by the `anthropic-messages`, `openai-completions`, `openai-responses` and `openai-codex-responses` adapters, the four protocols nax registers.

An HTTP error response has no `Retry-After` header, or a non-numeric one: `retryAfter` stays absent (`parseRetryAfter` returns undefined); `status` comes from the observed response. The underlying `fetch` rejects (no HTTP response): The rejection reaches pi-ai unchanged; `onResponse` is not called.

**Scope** — In: the new fetch observer, its production createPiDeps wiring, unit fetch semantics and real-pi error regression tests in `packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/error-response-fetch.test.ts`. Keep the existing real-pi thinking-budget suite unchanged. Out: final tool arguments (US-001), thinking buffering (US-002), credential shape/deadline (US-004), and picker filtering (US-005). The native retry policy in `packages/nax-agent` (`turnRetryDelayMs`, `isRetryableTransportFault`) is unchanged; it already honours `retryAfter`. An HTTP-date `Retry-After` value is not parsed; `parseRetryAfter` accepts seconds only, as today. pi-ai's own in-adapter request retries are not changed or configured. pi-ai's `anthropic-messages` federation client is rebuilt when the `fetch` it was built with changes; nax does not configure federation, so the per-request wrapper is not memoised.

**Interface** — `observeErrorResponses(onResponse)` returns a function with the signature of `globalThis.fetch`; `PiResponse` (`{ status, headers }`); `PiStreamFn`, whose fourth parameter is `onResponse`; `parseRetryAfter` and `statusFromSdkMessage` (from `./errors.ts`); `ProtocolStreamError.protocolError`.

Construct the wrapper before installing a fetch stub to pin call-time lookup. Real-pi integration tests construct createClient with defaultProviders(), transportRetries:0 and a protocols factory returning defaultProtocols({ credentials, providerOverrides }) over a memory store with an openai API key; select await client.model("openai", "gpt-5.4"). Restore globals after each test. Streamed 200-error controls must deliver SSE events in their own macrotasks. Verify error payloads rather than changing or exercising a real 41-second native wait. Demonstrate the lost Retry-After regression on baseline; do not change provider error classification.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] When observeErrorResponses(onResponse) is constructed before globalThis.fetch is stubbed to return HTTP 429 with Retry-After: 41, calling the wrapper resolves to that same Response object.

[unit] When observeErrorResponses(onResponse) is constructed before globalThis.fetch is stubbed to return HTTP 429 with Retry-After: 41, calling the wrapper calls onResponse once with status 429 and a plain headers record whose retry-after entry is 41 as a string.
[unit] When observeErrorResponses(onResponse) is called with a URL and an init object while globalThis.fetch is stubbed to return HTTP 429, the fetch stub receives exactly that URL and init object.
[unit] (control) When globalThis.fetch returns a 200 Response, the wrapper resolves to that Response.
[unit] (control) When globalThis.fetch returns a 200 Response, the wrapper never calls onResponse.
[unit] When globalThis.fetch rejects with new TypeError("network down"), the wrapper rejects with that same error.
[unit] When globalThis.fetch rejects with new TypeError("network down"), the wrapper never calls onResponse.

[integration] Through the real-pi client, when fetch returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After: 41 and a JSON error body, client.complete rejects with ProtocolStreamError whose protocolError has kind rate-limit, status 429 and retryAfter 41.

[integration] Through the real-pi client, when fetch returns HTTP 503 with Retry-After: 41 and a JSON error body, client.complete rejects with ProtocolStreamError whose protocolError has kind overloaded, status 503 and retryAfter 41.

[integration] (control) Through the real-pi client, when fetch returns HTTP 429 with no Retry-After header, client.complete rejects with ProtocolStreamError whose protocolError has status 429 and no retryAfter property.

[integration] (control) Through the real-pi client, when fetch returns HTTP 200 with Retry-After: 41 and a stream whose only event is response.failed with error code rate_limit, client.complete rejects with ProtocolStreamError whose protocolError has kind rate-limit and retryAfter 41.

[integration; failure handling] (control) Through the real-pi client, when fetch returns HTTP 429 with a non-numeric Retry-After header and a JSON error body, client.complete rejects with ProtocolStreamError whose protocolError has status 429 and no retryAfter property.

routing.reasoning: A small Node-compatible fetch adapter, one production wiring change and local real-pi tests restore metadata without modifying retry policy or authentication.

userStories.title: Refuse incompatible credential files and bound lock acquisition
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Prevent destructive rewrites of incompatible credential stores and make lockTimeoutMs a single acquisition deadline.

**Motivation** — A version 1 file whose credentials were an array, and a version 2 file, were both rewritten as version 1 with keys `"0"` and the new provider.

**Approach** — `readShape(path)` (`packages/nax-ai/src/credentials/file-store.ts`).
Target: additionally throws `The credential file at <path> is not a version 1 credential store. Refusing to overwrite it.` when `version` is not the number `1`, and the existing `could not be parsed as a credential store. Refusing to overwrite it.` error when `credentials` is null, an array, or not an object. Neither message includes file content. `read`, `modify` and `delete` all go through `readShape`, so each throws on such a file and `modify` writes nothing.

`withLock(fn)` in `createFileCredentialStore` (`packages/nax-ai/src/credentials/file-store.ts`).
Target: acquisition runs against one deadline, `lockTimeoutMs` after the first attempt. Each attempt calls `lockfile.lock` with `retries: 0`. On `ELOCKED`, if the deadline has passed it throws the existing `Timed out waiting for the credential file lock at <path>. Another process is holding it.` error with the `ELOCKED` error as `cause`; otherwise it sleeps the next backoff (starting at 20 ms, growing by 1.6, never past the time left to the deadline) and tries again. Any other error propagates as today. `DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` (5000) and `STALE_MS` are unchanged.

The credential file has `version` 2, or a credentials array: `read`, `modify` and `delete` throw; the file is left byte-for-byte unchanged. The lock is held past `lockTimeoutMs`: `modify` throws the `Timed out waiting for the credential file lock` error and the callback never runs.

Preserve ENOENT's empty-store behavior, invalid-JSON refusal without exposing parse content, atomic writes, owner-only modes, create-only initialization, lock release in finally and cross-process serialization. Check the acquisition deadline before retrying after sleep so a lock released too late cannot be acquired. The deadline does not limit work inside a successfully acquired lock.

**Scope** — In: readShape validation and withLock acquisition in the same file, with new incompatible-file and deadline suites. Keep the existing file-store suite unchanged. Out: protocol tool/thinking/HTTP changes (US-001 through US-003) and picker filtering (US-005). The individual credential entries inside a valid version 1 map are not validated. No migration from another version or from an array layout is added; such a file is refused, not converted. `STALE_MS` and the stale-lock breaking behaviour of proper-lockfile are unchanged. A `lockTimeoutMs` of 0 or below is not newly validated. `nax auth list` keeps its own looser check of the credential file (`readStoredEntries` in `packages/nax-agent/src/native/credentials/index.ts`), so it may list a provider from a file the store now refuses to read.

**Interface** — `readShape(path)`; `withLock(fn)`; `createFileCredentialStore({ path })`; `lockTimeoutMs`; `read`, `modify` and `delete`. The version 1 store has a credentials map. A version 2 fixture is {"version":2,"credentials":{"existing":{"kind":"api-key","key":"k"}}}; an array fixture is {"version":1,"credentials":[{"providerId":"existing","kind":"api-key","key":"k"}]}.

Use fresh temp directories per case, the existing barrier/cleanup patterns, and coordinated competing modify calls. Measure the second acquisition from its start, release the first writer in finally and settle both calls before cleanup. New files are file-store-shape.test.ts and file-store-lock-deadline.test.ts. Security-critical credential code requires strict three-session TDD: the test-writing session changes no source; the implementation session does not change tests; a verifier confirms regressions fail on old code and valid-store/lock controls stay intact.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Given the version 2 fixture, modify("new", ...) rejects with a message containing is not a version 1 credential store and Refusing to overwrite it.
[unit] After that version 2 modify rejection, the file bytes equal the bytes written before the call.
[unit] Given the array fixture, modify("new", ...) rejects with a message containing could not be parsed as a credential store.
[unit] After that array-file modify rejection, the file bytes are unchanged.
[unit] Given the version 2 fixture, read("existing") rejects with the is not a version 1 credential store error.
[unit] Given {"version":1,"credentials":null}, modify("new", ...) rejects with the could not be parsed as a credential store error.
[unit] Given {"credentials":{}} with no version, modify("new", ...) rejects with the is not a version 1 credential store error.
[unit] Rejection messages for the version 2 fixture and array fixture do not disclose their stored key k.
[unit] (control) Given a version 1 credentials map holding existing, modify("new", ...) resolves.
[unit] (control) After that valid version 1 modify, the file holds both existing and new with version 1.

[unit] With lockTimeoutMs 20, when a first modify("a", ...) holds the lock and releases it 80 ms after a second modify("b", ...) starts, the second call rejects with Timed out waiting for the credential file lock.
[unit] In that 20 ms deadline case, the second modify callback never runs.

[unit] With lockTimeoutMs 200 and a first modify holding the lock until the second call settles, the second modify rejects with Timed out waiting for the credential file lock less than 400 ms after it started.
[unit] (control) With lockTimeoutMs 1000, when the first modify releases the lock 50 ms after a second modify("b", ...) starts, the second call resolves.
[unit] (control) After that successful within-deadline acquisition, the file holds b.
[unit] (control) With no lockTimeoutMs, an uncontended modify("a", ...) resolves.
[unit] (control) After that default-timeout uncontended modify, the file holds a.
[unit; failure handling] Given the array fixture, read("existing") rejects with the could not be parsed as a credential store error.
[unit; failure handling] Given the version 2 fixture, delete("existing") rejects with the is not a version 1 credential store error.
[unit; failure handling] Given the array fixture, delete("existing") rejects with the could not be parsed as a credential store error.
[unit; failure handling] After read("existing") or delete("existing") rejects for either incompatible fixture, the file remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

routing.reasoning: Two bounded fixes in one store plus two regression suites; credential integrity, secret-safe errors and concurrent refresh locking mandate strict security TDD isolation regardless of size.

userStories.title: Offer only runnable discovered catalog models
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Exclude discovered catalog models whose protocols the native client does not register, while preserving explicit local declarations.

**Motivation** — A selected Google model failed with `Unknown protocol`, because the native client registers only `DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_NAMES` and `listCatalogModels` filters on `supportsTools` alone.

**Approach** — `listCatalogModels(providerIds)` (`packages/nax/src/agents/catalog/index.ts`).
Target: also requires `DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_NAMES` (imported from `@nathapp/nax-ai`) to include `model.protocol`. Order, the `supportsTools` filter and the empty result on a catalog load failure are unchanged.

`packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-protocols.ts`: `DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_NAMES` (`anthropic-messages`, `openai-completions`, `openai-responses`, `openai-codex-responses`), exported from `@nathapp/nax-ai`.
`packages/nax-ai/src/providers/types.ts`: `ResolvedModel.protocol` (string) and `ResolvedModel.supportsTools`.
`packages/nax/src/chat/chat-models.ts`: `chatModelChoices(input)`, which appends `input.listCatalogModels(input.availableProviders)` after the configured tiers and `catalogOverrides`. Unchanged.
`packages/nax/src/cli/chat.ts`: `discoverModels` passes the production `listCatalogModels` to `chatModelChoices`. Unchanged.

`packages/nax/test/unit/agents/catalog/list-models.test.ts` — its `provider(id)` fixture gives every model `protocol: "test"`, which `DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_NAMES` does not include, so AC-1 to AC-3 would list nothing. The invariant: the fixture's models (and `defaultProtocol`) use `openai-completions`, and AC-1 to AC-4 keep their expected lists and call counts.

**Scope** — In: the catalog boundary's filter, fixture protocol correction, and a new list-models-protocol.test.ts suite that passes production listCatalogModels to chatModelChoices. Out: final-tool, thinking, HTTP and credential-store fixes (US-001 through US-004). Configured tier models and `agent.native.catalogOverrides` entries stay in the picker regardless of protocol, because they are explicit local declarations. The native client's registered protocols are not read at runtime; the picker uses `DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_NAMES`, which is what `buildNativeClient` registers. Do not add providers or protocols or edit chatModelChoices/discoverModels.

**Interface** — `listCatalogModels(providerIds)`; `_catalogDeps`; `chatModelChoices(input)`; `DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_NAMES`; `ResolvedModel.protocol` (string) and `ResolvedModel.supportsTools`.

Use bun:test and the existing _catalogDeps seam, restoring it after each test. The standard fixture provider p1 contains m1 (openai-completions, tools), m2 (google-generative-ai, tools), m3 (anthropic-messages, no tools) and m4 (openai-responses, tools). Keep cache-per-loader semantics and provider/catalog order; import DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_NAMES only within the existing catalog boundary. Demonstrate the unsupported-protocol regression fails before adding the filter; retain existing expected lists and load counts after correcting fixture protocols.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Given p1 models m1 (openai-completions, tools), m2 (google-generative-ai, tools), m3 (anthropic-messages, no tools) and m4 (openai-responses, tools), listCatalogModels(["p1"]) returns ["p1/m1", "p1/m4"].
[unit] When every p1 model uses google-generative-ai, listCatalogModels(["p1"]) returns [].
[unit] (control) When p1 models use openai-codex-responses and anthropic-messages and both support tools, listCatalogModels(["p1"]) returns both in catalog order.
[unit] (control) When _catalogDeps.loadProviders rejects, listCatalogModels(["p1"]) returns [].
[unit] Given a config with no tiers and no overrides, availableProviders ["p1"] and the production listCatalogModels over the standard stubbed p1 catalog, chatModelChoices returns ["p1/m1", "p1/m4"].

analysis:
Discovery and scope: This is a narrowly scoped correction of review 0b834ecc1 findings 3, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11, not a new provider architecture. The codebase-memory MCP tools were unavailable in this host, so discovery used direct source reads and text searches rooted at /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax. The baseline implementation matches the spec's defect descriptions. Exactly five stories are retained, with US-002 depending only on US-001 because they edit the same stream state machine. US-003 also edits pi-client.ts independently; preserve neighboring story changes when integrating. No cross-story new API seam is required. Only packages/nax-ai and packages/nax need implementation changes; nax-agent and nax-agent-acp stay unchanged. All paths in this PRD are repository-relative, including each story's new test files.

Architecture and constraints: packages/nax-ai/package.json:38 pins pi-ai 1.5.0 and proper-lockfile 4.1.2; its scripts at :22-33 use Vitest, Node-compatible TypeScript builds and import/runtime gates. packages/nax-ai/vitest.config.ts:5 includes test/**/*.test.ts in a Node environment and excludes live tests. Source must remain Node >=22.19 compatible, with explicit .ts relative imports and exactOptionalPropertyTypes conditional properties. pi-ai imports are confined to pi-client.ts, pi-catalog.ts and pi-auth.ts; the new error-response-fetch.ts must import no pi-ai and use no Bun APIs. Credentials and reasoning signatures remain opaque, with no logging, parsing or synthesis of their values. The nax package is Bun-native, uses bun:test and dependency seams, and allows nax-ai imports only inside src/agents/catalog/. docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:13 and :168 summarize the coding standards and package graph. No public exports, dependency versions or release metadata need to change. The implementation does not initiate a lockstep release.

US-001 baseline and impact: packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-client.ts:342 defines createPiProtocol, and :411 parses only the delta accumulator in toolcall_end. packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/tool-args.ts:20 accumulates by call id; :51 returns {} for empty text and JSON.parse otherwise. The target must still parse first so malformed deltas retain the existing drain/error path even if completed arguments are valid. After parsing succeeds, prefer event.toolCall.arguments only with no argumentsError and a non-null, non-array object; otherwise retain the parsed accumulation. This changes final tool-call input, not tool-call-partial deltas. It fixes completed-item-only and corrected-final-argument cases without changing unknown tool handling or grammar-tool specialization. packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/pi-client-tool-args.test.ts:21-76 supplies fakePi, message and drain patterns; :83-193 covers usage, drain suppression, aborts and thrown failures. Existing matching-delta and malformed-delta tests need no modification. Create pi-client-final-args.test.ts with both scripted tests and real-pi local SSE tests; a pure mapper test alone cannot prove pi-ai actually delivers the terminal correction.

US-002 baseline and impact: packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-client.ts:328 reads optional signature/redacted metadata at a content index; :385 emits thinking immediately at thinking_end, before the final response can backfill encrypted_content. Hold immutable values plus contentIndex in arrival order, then copy terminal metadata only on normal done (:433). Preserve thinking_end text, retain early fields when terminal metadata is absent, and do not inspect signatures. The drain branch at :356, error path at :460, loop exhaustion at :494 and catch at :495 all need deliberate fallback flushing. Flush before any usage/error emitted by those endings; drain done must not use terminal enrichment. On an aborted error preserve non-zero usage then rethrow the signal reason without flushing; on a thrown failure with an aborted signal rethrow the thrown failure without flushing. Do not move thinking-delta emission. Clear or consume held blocks so no path emits them twice. Risks are changed complete-block event ordering, losing blocks on less-common exits, leaking held blocks on abort, or duplicate flushing through catch. Tool-call completion can now precede complete thinking, while replayed assistant content still puts thinking first in toPiMessages at :202. packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/collect.ts:68-79 appends thinking in arrival order and derives CompleteResult, so it must remain unchanged; :20 exposes ProtocolStreamError.protocolError and preserves billed usage. Existing tests at packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/pi-client.test.ts:475-552 assert presence/metadata, not the old timing, and their done messages lack thinking, so they remain unchanged. Create pi-client-terminal-thinking.test.ts with distinct partial and terminal objects to prevent shared mutation from hiding the bug. The two-request real-pi test must verify store:false and encrypted_content replay, with one SSE event per macrotask. This is opaque encrypted-signature replay, so use strict three-session TDD isolation.

US-003 baseline and impact: packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-client.ts:1064 builds production dependencies; :1129-1142 passes onResponse but no fetch override. On HTTP SDK failures that callback is bypassed. :460-485 already classifies errors from observed status and parseRetryAfter(observed.headers), falling back to statusFromSdkMessage; adding observation before SDK processing is sufficient. New observeErrorResponses must read globalThis.fetch at invocation rather than capture it at construction, forward arguments exactly, preserve response identity and body, observe >=400 only, and propagate rejection identity. Keep pi-ai's successful-response onResponse hook so a successful adapter retry overwrites a previous error observation. packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/errors.ts:11 classifies 429 as rate-limit and 503/529 as overloaded; :233 accepts numeric Retry-After seconds only. Do not modify classification or retry policy. packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/retry.ts:81 retries only transport faults before any event; a thinking or usage event already prevents internal retry. packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/turn-retry.ts:66-73 accepts transport, overloaded and rate-limit, and :109-119 already converts retryAfter seconds to milliseconds and caps to remaining turn budget. Therefore no nax-agent code changes or 41-second real sleeps are necessary. New error-response-fetch.test.ts must test the wrapper and the actual createClient/defaultProtocols wiring using a memory credential store and stubbed fetch, not an injected PiDeps substitute. packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/pi-client-thinking-budget.test.ts:26-77 demonstrates real-pi construction, providerOverrides forwarding, fetch stubbing, transportRetries:0 and global cleanup. Keep its existing 401 assertion unchanged. Account for pi-ai's own retry attempts without changing their configuration.

US-004 baseline and impact: packages/nax-ai/src/credentials/file-store.ts:61-82 parses JSON but only checks for an object with a credentials property, allowing arrays and other versions to reach modify. Introduce version===1 validation plus non-null, non-array object validation of credentials, using the distinct specified secret-free messages and never attaching JSON parse content as a cause. ENOENT remains EMPTY. read at :152 reads readShape directly, modify at :156-169 reads it under withLock, and delete at :172 delegates to modify, so all three operations must refuse incompatible files. writeShape at :91-111 atomically renames same-directory temp files, uses create-only hard linking during initialization, and enforces file mode 0600; preserve it and directory mode 0700. ensureFile at :120-123 must not replace an existing incompatible file. No migration is added: legitimate v1 maps continue unchanged, while unsupported/corrupt layouts are refused for operator repair, byte-for-byte intact. Individual credential entries are intentionally not validated. Security risk is secret disclosure in errors or silent credential loss; strict three-session TDD applies.

The lock defect is at packages/nax-ai/src/credentials/file-store.ts:126-143: proper-lockfile receives ten retries with lockTimeoutMs as maxTimeout, so the option bounds each retry sleep rather than total acquisition. Replace this with one deadline beginning at the first acquisition attempt, retries:0 on each call, ELOCKED-only backoff starting at 20ms with factor 1.6, clamped to remaining time. Recheck the deadline before a later attempt so a lock released after the deadline cannot be acquired. Keep the latest ELOCKED as timeout cause, propagate other errors unchanged, and release an acquired lock in finally (:145-149). The deadline applies to acquisition, not callback execution or a Promise.race that could leave a late acquisition behind. DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS remains 5000 and STALE_MS remains 10000. packages/nax-ai/test/credentials/file-store.test.ts:20-35 has temp-dir/barrier cleanup patterns; :150-176 pins refusal, release and secret safety; :180-221 pins real cross-process serialization. Add separate shape and deadline suites without modifying that existing suite. Coordinate the first writer entering its callback before starting the second, always release barriers in finally, and await both writers before deleting temp directories. Verify real elapsed acquisition times with the specified tolerances; do not let delayed scheduling or an unhandled rejection invalidate the deadline test.

US-005 baseline and impact: packages/nax/src/agents/catalog/index.ts:29 already owns the permitted nax-ai import boundary, :75 exposes _catalogDeps, and :99-121 caches per loader identity and deduplicates loads. :192-201 listCatalogModels currently filters supportsTools only. Add DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_NAMES membership there, without changing cache behavior, provider/catalog order, supportsTools filtering, or [] on load failure. DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_NAMES is already public at packages/nax-ai/src/index.ts:62 and defined as the four supported APIs at packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-protocols.ts:30-35; defaultProtocols registers exactly those names at :103-112. packages/nax-agent/src/native/client.ts:70-99 uses that defaultProtocols factory, so a static filter matches the production native registration without introducing a runtime registry query. packages/nax/src/chat/chat-models.ts:46-58 appends production catalog choices after tiers/overrides and deduplicates them; packages/nax/src/cli/chat.ts:310-324 derives available providers then forwards deps.listCatalogModels. These consumers remain unchanged. Explicit tiers and catalogOverrides must not be filtered by protocol. Existing packages/nax/test/unit/agents/catalog/list-models.test.ts:7-21 uses protocol/defaultProtocol test; change both to openai-completions or its existing tool/order/cache tests will intentionally fail under the new filter. Preserve its expected lists and call counts at :23-40. New list-models-protocol.test.ts must use a unique/restored _catalogDeps.loadProviders reference for each case and test chatModelChoices with the production listCatalogModels, not a prefiltered stub.

Compatibility, testing and completion: All six fixes are behavioral corrections with no API/schema migration. Correct credential maps, normal tool deltas, early reasoning signatures, successful HTTP observation, configured picker declarations, and existing cache/failure behavior are regression anchors. The intentional behavior changes are final tool input authority, later complete-thinking emission, restored retry hints, refusal of incompatible credential files, bounded contention waits, and omission of unsupported discovered protocols. packages/nax-agent/src/native/credentials/index.ts:173-216 still lists credentials without checking version, so auth list can disagree with the stricter store; leave that documented discrepancy untouched. New Vitest files mirror src under packages/nax-ai/test; nax's new catalog file uses bun:test and its existing dependency seam. Write regression tests first and demonstrate the relevant new regressions fail on old code, while recognizing control assertions already pass; no tests have been executed during PRD drafting because execution tools are not available here. Scripted pi events validate mapping, while real-pi plus local fetch validates upstream adapter integration, not live-provider behavior. Use createClient with defaultProviders(), transportRetries:0, memory openai API-key credentials and a protocols factory passing providerOverrides to defaultProtocols; select await client.model('openai','gpt-5.4'). Deliver SSE events in separate macrotasks so terminal mutation cannot make the baseline falsely pass, and restore stubbed globals after every test. Run package-scoped test commands and the existing pipeline gates, never bare bun test, never live provider tests, and never coverage inside NAX_SANDBOXED=1. Done means every preserved spec AC and failure-table behavior is demonstrated, existing controls remain intact, and no deferred review arcs, provider protocols, credential migration or native retry changes are introduced.

Refine-pass adversarial audit: Re-read spec.md:187-256 and the relevant current stream, credential-store, catalog, picker and test-harness source. All 46 numbered spec ACs remain in their original stories. The following exhaustive mapping uses 1-based acceptanceCriteria positions; split assertions preserve the original combined criterion rather than dropping part of it. US-001: spec 1->1 (corrected final KL), 2->2 (no deltas), 3->3 (matching-delta control), 4->4 (argumentsError fallback), 5->5 (malformed bad-request and exact lookup message), 6->6 (no tool-call control), 7->7 (real-pi completed-item-only arguments), 8->8 (real-pi correction). US-002: spec 1->1 (one final-signature block and separate message object), 2->2 (event-order suffix), 3->3 (early-metadata control with missing/wrong terminal block), 4->4 (terminal signature/redacted override), 5->5 (arrival order), 6->6 (error fallback with thinking_end values), 7->7 (nonterminal exhaustion fallback with thinking_end values), 8->8+9 (thinking before usage and final bad-request), 9->10 (thrown failure), 10->11+12 (same abort reason and no thinking), 11->13 (macrotask two-request replay, store false), 12->14 (encrypted_content replay), 13->15 (early encrypted_content control). US-003: spec 1->1+2 (post-construction fetch stub, response identity and callback payload), 2->3 (exact URL/init forwarding), 3->4+5 (200 response identity and no callback control), 4->6+7 (same rejection and no callback), 5->8 (429 kind/status/retryAfter), 6->9 (503 kind/status/retryAfter), 7->10 (no-header absence control), 8->11 (200 streamed rate_limit control). US-004: spec 1->1 (version refusal message), 2->2 (original bytes), 3->3+4 (array refusal and original bytes), 4->5 (version refusal on read), 5->6 (null map refusal), 6->7 (missing version refusal), 7->8 (stored-key secrecy), 8->9+10 (valid-map success and preserved entries/version control), 9->11+12 (20ms timeout and no callback), 10->13 (200ms deadline with <400ms bound), 11->14+15 (50ms release/acquisition and stored b control), 12->16+17 (default uncontended success and stored a control). US-005: spec 1->1 (mixed protocols/tools), 2->2 (all unsupported), 3->3 (both registered in catalog order control), 4->4 (load failure empty control), 5->5 (production listCatalogModels composed into chatModelChoices). All control markers and qualifying clauses, including retained thinking_end values, separate terminal objects, catalog order, absence rather than undefined properties, unchanged bytes and timing bounds, survive.

Failure-table audit: row 1 maps to US-001 criteria 5/6/9 (unchanged malformed-argument handling and terminal usage ordering); row 2 to US-001 criterion 4 (argumentsError fallback); row 3 to US-002 criteria 6-10/16-18 (error/drain/throw flushing, with abort exceptions retained in 11/12/19-21); row 4 to US-003 criteria 10/12 (missing and non-numeric Retry-After); row 5 to US-003 criteria 6/7 and production fetch wiring (rejection identity/no observation); row 6 to US-004 criteria 1-8/18-21 (all incompatible-file operations and byte preservation); row 7 to US-004 criteria 11-13 (bounded lock failure and no callback). Every story has a directly observable negative path and backward-compatibility controls, so no speculative extra acceptance criterion was needed. Existing supplementary criteria derive from explicit design/failure requirements. Context audit: US-001 retains all four spec-recommended files, US-002 all five, US-003 all four, US-004 both, and US-005 all three plus the CLI and protocol-name reference; none is a file the same story creates. The only dependency remains the binding US-002->US-001, and all ids resolve. All 17 feature-level exclusions are retained verbatim in outOfScope, including the US-specific items that occur before Stories; the excluded final-empty-argument state is also echoed into US-001 scope without adding an AC for it. Corrections made during audit: thinking metadata criteria now locate fields in partial.content/contentIndex and done.message.content rather than suggesting root-level fields; the repeated thinking-failure summary and supplementary drain criteria explicitly respect the abort exception; malformed-usage ordering retains its unchanged-behavior qualification; US-002 is medium because its changes stay in one existing stream module, with the encrypted-signature security override retaining strict three-session TDD. Other routing remains medium with standard TDD except security-critical credential storage, which retains strict three-session TDD. This audit is a source/spec review, not an execution result.
outOfScope: Findings 1, 2 and 4-6, 12-17 and 19-22 of review 0b834ecc belong to the other review-0b834 features (agent-acp, release-config-ci and workflow-verification), which are merged; finding 18 was withdrawn as a CLI defect.
No live provider was shown to emit the finding 3 or finding 7 sequences; the fixes are verified against local responses only, and no live test is added.
US-001 only: a custom (grammar) tool call is not given separate handling; its `toolcall_end` takes `toolCall.arguments` under the same rule as a JSON call.

US-001 only: no AC covers deltas that parse to a non-empty object while `toolCall.arguments` is `{}` with no `argumentsError`; pi-ai 1.5.0 replaces the delta text only when the completed item's arguments are non-empty, so it does not produce that state, and the rule then emits `{}`.
US-001 only: a tool call whose accumulated delta text is not JSON still ends the stream with the `bad-request` error, even when pi-ai's completed arguments are valid.
US-002 only: `thinking-delta` events are still emitted as they arrive; only the complete `thinking` block moves to the end of the stream.
US-003 only: the native retry policy in `packages/nax-agent` (`turnRetryDelayMs`, `isRetryableTransportFault`) is unchanged; it already honours `retryAfter`.
US-003 only: an HTTP-date `Retry-After` value is not parsed; `parseRetryAfter` accepts seconds only, as today.
US-003 only: pi-ai's own in-adapter request retries are not changed or configured.
US-004 only: the individual credential entries inside a valid version 1 map are not validated.
US-004 only: no migration from another version or from an array layout is added; such a file is refused, not converted.
US-004 only: `STALE_MS` and the stale-lock breaking behaviour of proper-lockfile are unchanged.
US-004 only: a `lockTimeoutMs` of 0 or below is not newly validated.
US-005 only: configured tier models and `agent.native.catalogOverrides` entries stay in the picker regardless of protocol, because they are explicit local declarations.
US-005 only: the native client's registered protocols are not read at runtime; the picker uses `DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_NAMES`, which is what `buildNativeClient` registers.

US-004 only: `nax auth list` keeps its own looser check of the credential file (`readStoredEntries` in `packages/nax-agent/src/native/credentials/index.ts`), so it may list a provider from a file the store now refuses to read.
US-003 only: pi-ai's `anthropic-messages` federation client is rebuilt when the `fetch` it was built with changes; nax does not configure federation, so the per-request wrapper is not memoised.
